answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than to free account creation: a new agent starts with almost no transaction capacity and must complete checked jobs to earn it, like a vine that only climbs after putting down roots. Each identity posts a refundable stake that is slashed if the same operator is caught running clones, so creating thousands of fakes costs real money up front. A shared registry records work histories, so a fresh identity cannot inherit trust, standing as exposed as shale on a lagoon shore until it builds its own record.
